results.question: how should I warm up for tendonitis?
results.answer: For tendonitis, warm up your joints properly before any heavy work, and build the load gradually—tendons adapt more slowly than muscles. Isometric holds under load can also help build tendon strength. Make sure to take it easy if your tendons feel tender, and consider a physio for tailored advice.

results.question: what should I do for my tendons when I lift my shoulders?
results.answer: For your tendons when lifting your shoulders, focus on warm-up and controlled movement. Keep the load light at first, and only go as far as your shoulder allows without pain. Avoid sharp pinching or pushing through discomfort. Let your tendons adapt slowly — they take time to strengthen.
